capability.title: Open Frontier
capability.question: How does it work? What can I build and verify?
capability.purpose: Explain mechanisms, construct models, measure uncertainty and build systems that survive contact with physical reality.

context.title: Human Worlds
context.question: How do people and institutions actually work?
context.purpose: Enter unfamiliar societies and historical situations, reconstruct actors' meanings, compare explanations and trace institutions, incentives and power.

judgment.title: Philosophy
judgment.question: What should I believe, value and do?
judgment.purpose: Reconstruct arguments, expose assumptions, examine rival accounts and defend judgments about knowledge, value, meaning and legitimacy.

representation.title: Expressive Command
representation.question: How can I interpret, articulate and give form to understanding?
representation.purpose: Read and listen closely, express ideas with precision, and make language, images, space and material form answerable to meaning and use.

learning.title: Learning to learn
learning.question: How do I become more capable of independent learning?
learning.purpose: Investigate attention, memory, practice, motivation and judgment. Use evidence of retention and transfer rather than familiarity or confidence alone.

TS-F01.title: Mathematical reasoning and proof
TS-F01.question: When does an argument establish a claim, rather than merely make it plausible?
TS-F01.first_attempt: Negate 'Every tested component is safe.' Give an example where many successful tests fail to establish safety. Explain the missing inference.

HW05.title: Collective action and the commons
HW05.question: Why can people who share an interest still fail to act together?
HW05.first_attempt: Describe a shared resource you know. Separate who can use it, who maintains it, who sets its rules and who can appeal a decision.

EX-M11.title: Reading literature as a whole work
EX-M11.question: How does a work's form change what can be understood, felt and said?
EX-M11.first_attempt: Read a short dramatic scene aloud twice with different emphasis. Identify an interpretation that changes and the words that support it.
